summary: All four pinned pre-scan blockers resolved through the real compilation path, plus the two next blockers their repair exposed. (1) The 4 untraceable grid refusals are REPAIRED inside the declared launch contract (no protocol change, so no DESIGN_ISSUE): gn_finalize's (n,g) axes -- visible only as the view product n*g -- flatten to ONE axis over the product because the kernel's whole program-id surface is the C-order linear index pid_n*num_programs(1)+pid_g (gridmodel.linear_pid_root proves it from the TIR; apply_linear_flattening rewrites the expression to program_id(0); the (pid_n,pid_g)->linear bijection is the re-partition proof, F018); grouped_gemm's tile-count sum over the unsigned groups axis (one identity spans groups=3/4) lowers as a runtime SumLoop over the bundle-visible group_size scalar (neither count unrolled; the native grid routine loops the actual read). Repairing grouped_gemm exposed the next blocker on its path: a 64-bit unsigned scalar load emitted a zext sload with no repertoire row (extension is vacuous at 64 bits) -- fixed to sext like the entry binding. All 4 operators' cases execute and compare PASS at 1 and 4 workers (gn_finalize 3 shapes, grouped_gemm 2 shapes; one artifact per identity, runtime grid follows the bundle). (2) The deconv3d typical-case defect is fixed at the lowering stage (first incorrect stage: the MIR staging, not the emitter): [1]-element staged records (tl.full([1],...) products like Oy_i64*Ox_i64) were stored/read with the raw (elem+lane) index, writing vl lanes per pass far past the one-element allocation and smashing neighbouring staged regions -- the div/mod recomposition oz*(Oy*Ox) then read the smashed product back as Ox (every corpus shape has Oy==Ox, so the wrong factor coincided with a legal-looking value; the minimized reproduction uses Oy=10/Ox=14 to distinguish). Extent-1 records now stage element 0 (the register is the value's splat). All 6 deconv3d case rows (2 shapes x 3 dtypes) execute and compare PASS at 1 and 4 workers; the T037 pin flipped to a full comparison PASS. (3) The gqa 1-worker CSE segfault: the CSE rewrites are value-legal; the defect was the mis-shaped read -- the ptradd lowering materialized a staged BASE block via _need(base) with no consumer shape, so a staged [32,1] base consumed by a [32,32] ptradd was read with the raw identity index while the consumer pass's element counter ran past the base's extent (T029 had fixed only the offset side). The staged base read now maps through the result's shape. gqa executes and compares PASS at 1,2,4,8 workers with passes ON and OFF. (4) The fp64 tl.dot refusal's justification verified recorded: FRONTEND_COVERAGE.json's tl.dot row carries the T038 dtype-surface boundary note naming CORPUS_LOCK.json (per-operator dtypes float32/float16/bfloat16; global declared set has no float64), so the refusal reads as declared-unsupported with evidence. Stale pins that encoded the old refusal states were updated (test_t037/t034/atomics); the compile sweep's compilation unit was aligned with the driver's declared artifact key (identity + argument layout: grouped_gemm's group-count shapes legitimately split one identity into two layouts).
